Why <main> matters for accessibility

Screen reader users jump straight to <main>. Without it, they tab through nav and ads to find the content.

One <main> per page — visible, unique, dominant.

#a11y#html

    :last-childStructuralLast child of its parent.

    Part IV — Master Reference Tables · Global Attribute IndexPage 698 of 8000

    Global Attribute Index — part 1

    AttributeDescription
    accesskeyA keyboard shortcut (single character) that focuses/activates the element, e.g. accesskey="s" → Alt+S (Windows) / Ctrl-Option-S (macOS). Use sparingly — they collide with browser shortcuts.
    classOne or more space-separated class names. The backbone of CSS styling and JS queries: <p class="card dark">. Multiple classes: class="a b c".
    contenteditableMakes the element's content editable in place. true / false / plaintext-only. The browser shows a plain text-editing UI.
    data-…Custom data-* attributes for your own scripts. Must start with a letter, no uppercase. Read with el.dataset.name (camelCase).
    dirForces text direction: ltr (left-to-right), rtl (right-to-left), or auto (detect from content). Useful for user-generated names/quotes.
    draggableWhether the element can be dragged (HTML5 Drag & Drop API). true / false. Default true for images and links.
    hiddenRemoves the element from rendering (display:none). Can be overridden by CSS. Browsers respect it even before CSS loads — a11y-safe hiding.
    inertThe element and its descendants are non-interactive and invisible to assistive technology (greyed out). Great for disabling sidebars while a modal is open.
    inputmodeHint for the mobile virtual keyboard: none, text, search, tel, url, email, numeric, decimal, telephone. No effect on desktop.
    isThe name of a custom element to upgrade this built-in element to (tagged custom elements, e.g. <article is="my-card">).
    itemidPart of (the deprecated) microdata: a unique identifier for an item.
    itempropMicrodata: the property name of an item (e.g. itemprop="name").
    itemscopeMicrodata: makes this element the scope of a new item.
    itemtypeMicrodata: the URL of the schema the item follows.
    langThe language of the element's content (BCP-47). Used by screen readers to switch pronunciation and by spellcheckers. Inheritable.
    nonceA cryptographic nonce used with Content Security Policy to allow specific inline scripts/styles.
    partCSS Part API: exposes a part of the element to ::part() styling from outside a shadow DOM.
    popoverMakes the element a native popover: auto or hint. Toggled with element.showPopover().
    ← Prev Page 698 / 8000 · Global Attribute Index Next → Go to 🗺 Map
    Part IV — Master Reference Tables · Global Attribute IndexPage 699 of 8000

    Global Attribute Index — part 2

    AttributeDescription
    roleARIA: overrides/declares the accessible role (e.g. role="alert", role="presentation"). Prefer native elements first.
    slotAssigns the element to a named <slot> in a shadow DOM template.
    spellcheckWhether spellcheck applies: true / false. Inheritable — set it once on <html>.
    styleInline CSS declarations for this one element. Prefer classes; use for dynamic values only.
    tabindexControls keyboard focus order: 0 = focusable in DOM order, positive = custom order (avoid), -1 = focusable via JS only (not by Tab).
    titleAdvisory tooltip text on hover. A fallback, not an information channel — important info must be visible.
    translateWhether machine translation applies: yes / no. Use no on brand names and code.
    autocapitalizeMobile keyboards: off / sentences / words / characters — auto-capitalization behavior.
    autofocusFocus this element when the page loads. At most one per page; can hurt mobile/keyboard UX if abused.
    checkedDefault state of checkboxes/radios (HTML-only; change with JS .checked).
    disabledDisables a form control: not clickable, not submitted, greyed by default.
    readonlyA form control is selectable but cannot be edited; its value still submits.
    requiredThe control must have a valid value before the form can submit (native validation).
    selectedPre-selects an <option> in a <select> (HTML default state).
    valueThe current value of inputs/outputs: text, number, date, file…
    nameThe submitted key for form controls (and radios group by name).
    idA unique identifier within the document — used by CSS #id, href="#id", for=, and getElementById. Must be unique per page.
    aria-…Any ARIA attribute (aria-label, aria-expanded, aria-hidden, aria-live…) adds accessibility semantics when native HTML is not enough.

    Glossary — part 1 of 21

    TermDefinition
    <b>attribute</b>A name/value pair inside an opening tag (href, class, src…) that configures the element.
    <b>autofill</b>Browser feature that pre-fills form controls (name, email, card) from saved data; steered by the autocomplete attribute.
    <b>backdrop</b>The dimmed layer behind an open <dialog> (showModal) or a glassmorphism surface (backdrop-filter).
    <b>baseline</b>The invisible line on which text sits; inline elements align to the text baseline by default.
    <b>block formatting context</b>A layout container where children are laid out block-wise, isolated from the outside (created by BFC triggers like overflow:hidden).
    <b>border-box</b>Box model where width includes padding + border (the * { box-sizing: border-box; } reset).
    ← Prev Page 700 / 8000 · Glossary Next → Go to 🗺 Map
    Part V — Study: Glossary, Cheat Sheets & Quizzes · GlossaryPage 701 of 8000

    Glossary — part 2 of 21

    TermDefinition
    <b>browser engine</b>The rendering core (Blink, WebKit, Gecko) that parses HTML, computes style, and paints pixels.
    <b>cascade</b>The algorithm that resolves conflicting CSS rules using origin, layer, specificity, and source order.
    <b>checkbox</b>A multi-choice <input type="checkbox"> control (0..n selected).
    <b>class selector</b>The .name selector matching an element's class list — the backbone of styling.
    <b>clip-path</b>CSS that clips an element to a shape (circle, polygon, path) — non-rectangular UI.
    <b>color scheme</b>The declared light/dark support (color-scheme) that themes native controls and canvases.
    ← Prev Page 701 / 8000 · Glossary Next → Go to 🗺 Map
    Part V — Study: Glossary, Cheat Sheets & Quizzes · GlossaryPage 702 of 8000

    Glossary — part 3 of 21

    TermDefinition
    <b>combinator</b>Selector operators: space (descendant), > (child), + (adjacent sibling), ~ (general sibling).
    <b>component</b>A self-contained UI piece (card, modal) with its own markup, styles, and behavior.
    <b>computed style</b>The final values of a property after the cascade + inheritance (getComputedStyle).
    <b>contain</b>A CSS performance hint limiting an element's side effects to its subtree.
    <b>content box</b>The innermost rectangle of the box model — the area the width/height describe (content-box).
    <b>critical rendering path</b>HTML parse → DOM → CSS parse → CSSOM → render tree → layout → paint; the steps to a painted page.
    ← Prev Page 702 / 8000 · Glossary Next → Go to 🗺 Map

    <b>datalist</b>The <datalist> suggestions source linked to an <input> via list=…

    <b>edge-to-edge</b>Full-viewport layout where content reaches the screen edges (modern mobile design).
    <b>ellipsis truncation</b>The white-space:nowrap + overflow:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis one-line cut.

    <b>figure</b>The <figure> + <figcaption> pair for self-contained media with captions.

    <b>root element</b>The <html> element — the top of the DOM; rem's reference point.
    <b>RTL</b>Right-to-left writing direction (Arabic, Hebrew) — dir=rtl, logical properties.
    <b>sanitization</b>Cleaning untrusted input before it touches the DOM (XSS defense).

    TermDefinition
    <b>typographic scale</b>A harmonious font-size system (e.g. 1.25 ratio: 14→16→20→25).
    <b>underlay</b>A layer behind content (background effects, glows).
    <b>universal selector</b>* — every element; the reset's starting point.
    <b>valid HTML</b>Markup that parses per the spec (validators, browsers' error recovery).
    <b>variable font</b>One file, a range of weights/widths (font-variation-settings axes).
    <b>view-box</b>The SVG coordinate system the drawing scales into.
    ← Prev Page 717 / 8000 · Glossary Next → Go to 🗺 Map

    Glossary — part 19 of 21

    TermDefinition
    <b>viewport</b>The visible area of the page (the device's screen region showing the page).
    <b>vtt</b>WebVTT — the text track format for <track> captions/subtitles.
    <b>web component</b>A custom element + shadow DOM + template — a reusable encapsulated widget.
    <b>webfont</b>A font served over the web (@font-face) — woff2 preferred.
    <b>wbr</b>The word-break opportunity element for long URLs/words.
    <b>web vitals</b>The Core Web Vitals: LCP (loading), CLS (stability), INP (interaction).
    ← Prev Page 718 / 8000 · Glossary Next → Go to 🗺 Map

    Glossary — part 20 of 21

    TermDefinition
    <b>will-change</b>A layer-promotion hint for upcoming animations — use sparingly.
    <b>word-break</b>Where long words may break (CJK & overflow control).
    <b>writing mode</b>The text flow direction (horizontal-tb, vertical-rl) — CJK layouts.
    <b>x-height</b>The height of lowercase letters (no ascenders) — an ex/typography unit.
    <b>XML</b>The extensible markup language HTML descended from (XHTML era).
    <b>XSS</b>Cross-Site Scripting — injecting script via unsanitized input.

    Glossary — part 21 of 21

    TermDefinition
    <b>z-index</b>Stacking order for positioned elements (higher paints on top).
    <b>zebra striping</b>Alternating row backgrounds: tr:nth-child(even) — table readability.
    <b>zoom units</b>The vw/vh viewport length family (1vw = 1% of viewport width).
    <b>0 / 100vh mobile bug</b>Why 100vh jumps with the mobile browser UI — use dvh/svh/lvh.

    Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1Page 878 of 8000

    Drill 1 — html × min-width

    html min-width

    Apply min-width to <html> — the root element of every html document. The lower limit of the width.

    1 · The element

    <html> as rendered
    <html> → <head> + <body>

    2 · Starter code

    <html lang="en">
  <head>...</head>
  <body>...</body>
</html>

    3 · Your task

    • Write one CSS rule that applies min-width = 0 to the element.
    • Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.

    4 · Solution

    html {
  min-width: 0;
}

    5 · Value quick-quiz

Express (1 day, +$5)&lt;/label&gt; &lt;/fieldset&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>clip-path</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>fieldset { clip-path: …; “Matches elements that HAVE the attribute.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>[attr]</code></li><li>B. <code>:last-child</code></li><li>C. <code>:is(sel, …)</code></li><li>D. <code>:lang(code)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p988">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 989 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p990">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p990" data-page="990" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 113"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 990 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 113 — h1 × overflow-wrap</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">h1</span> <span class="badge prop">overflow-wrap</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">overflow-wrap</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;h1&gt;</code> — a section heading of importance level 1 (h1 = highest). Places an item in a grid area (shorthand for row/column start+end).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;dialog&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="width:240px;background:#fff;border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:10px;box-shadow:0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.18);padding:14px;font-size:13px"><b>Are you sure?</b><div style="margin-top:10px;text-align:right"><button style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;background:#f9fafb;border-radius:6px;padding:4px 10px;margin-right:6px;font-size:12px">Cancel</button><button style="border:none;background:#2563eb;color:#fff;border-radius:6px;padding:4px 12px;font-size:12px">OK</button></div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;dialog id=&quot;dlg&quot;&gt; &lt;form method=&quot;dialog&quot;&gt; &lt;p&gt;Are you sure?&lt;/p&gt; &lt;button value=&quot;cancel&quot;&gt;Cancel&lt;/button&gt; &lt;button formnovalidate&gt;OK&lt;/button&gt; &lt;/form&gt; &lt;/dialog&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>grid-area</b> = <b>name</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>dialog { grid-area: name; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The element is being pressed/clicked.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:where(sel, …)</code></li><li>B. <code>:target</code></li><li>C. <code>::first-line</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:active</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p991">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 992 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p993">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p993" data-page="993" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 116"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 993 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 116 — s × font-family</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">s</span> <span class="badge prop">font-family</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">font-family</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;s&gt;</code> — marks text that is no longer accurate or relevant (not a strikethrough for style). The typeface(s) to use, as a priority list.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;s&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">Price: <s style="color:#9ca3af">$99</s> <b>$79</b></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;Price: &lt;s&gt;$99&lt;/s&gt; $79&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>font-family</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>s { font-family: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The sole child of its parent.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:enabled / :disabled</code></li><li>B. <code>&gt;</code></li><li>C. <code>::marker</code></li><li>✔ D. <code>:only-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p992">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 993 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p994">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p994" data-page="994" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 117"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 994 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 117 — dfn × word-spacing</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">dfn</span> <span class="badge prop">word-spacing</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">word-spacing</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;dfn&gt;</code> — the term being defined on the page. Extra space between words.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;dfn&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px"><dfn style="font-style:italic"><b>semantics</b></dfn>: the meaning carried by markup, not just its appearance.</p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;&lt;dfn&gt;semantics&lt;/dfn&gt;: the meaning of markup.&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>word-spacing</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>dfn { word-spacing: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “First of its tag among siblings.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:placeholder-shown</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:first-of-type</code></li><li>C. <code>~</code></li><li>D. <code>::cue</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p993">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 994 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p995">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p995" data-page="995" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 118"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 995 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 118 — sup × white-space</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">sup</span> <span class="badge prop">white-space</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">white-space</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;sup&gt;</code> — superscript text (rendered above the baseline). How whitespace is handled: wrap, collapse, pre…</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;sup&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><p style="margin:0;font-size:13px">E = mc<sup>2</sup></p></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;p&gt;E = mc&lt;sup&gt;2&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>white-space</b> = <b>pre</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>sup { white-space: pre; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Everything EXCEPT the selector inside.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>:lang(code)</code></li><li>B. <code>::first-letter</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:not(sel)</code></li><li>D. <code>.class</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p994">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 995 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p996">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p996" data-page="996" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 119"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 996 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 119 — ol × background-color</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">ol</span> <span class="badge prop">background-color</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">background-color</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;ol&gt;</code> — a numbered list of items. The solid background color.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;ol&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><ol start="2" style="font-size:13px;margin:0;padding-left:22px;line-height:1.7"><li>Second step</li><li>Third step</li></ol></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;ol start=&quot;2&quot;&gt; &lt;li&gt;Second step&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Third step&lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ol&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>background-color</b> = <b>color</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>ol { background-color: color; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Parent selector! Matches if it CONTAINS the selector.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:has(sel)</code></li><li>B. <code>descendant (space)</code></li><li>C. <code>::placeholder</code></li><li>D. <code>[attr=value]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p995">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 996 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p997">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p997" data-page="997" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 120"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 997 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 120 — source × print-color-adjust</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">source</span> <span class="badge prop">print-color-adjust</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">print-color-adjust</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;source&gt;</code> — a candidate resource for &lt;video&gt;, &lt;audio&gt; or &lt;picture&gt;. Keep background colors when printing (-webkit-print-color-adjust).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;source&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;background:#f6f8fa;border:1px solid #d0d7de;border-radius:6px;padding:8px">1) movie.webm ✓ plays<br>2) movie.mp4 (fallback, skipped)</div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;video controls&gt; &lt;source src=&quot;movie.webm&quot; type=&quot;video/webm&quot;&gt; &lt;source src=&quot;movie.mp4&quot; type=&quot;video/mp4&quot;&gt; &lt;/video&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>print-color-adjust</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>source { print-color-adjust: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Field required or not.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::before</code></li><li>B. <code>::file-selector-button</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>:required / :optional</code></li><li>D. <code>[attr*=…]</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p996">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 997 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p998">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p998" data-page="998" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 121"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 998 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 121 — iframe × list-style-image</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">iframe</span> <span class="badge prop">list-style-image</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">list-style-image</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;iframe&gt;</code> — embeds another html page in a nested browsing context. Use an image (URL/SVG/data URI) as the list marker.</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;iframe&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="border:2px solid #8b949e;border-radius:6px;width:250px;padding:8px;background:#fff"><h1 style="font-size:14px;margin:2px 0 0">Hello from an iframe</h1><div style="font-size:10px;color:#8b949e">separate document, own DOM</div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;iframe srcdoc=&quot;&lt;h1&gt;Hello from an iframe&lt;/h1&gt;&quot; width=&quot;260&quot; height=&quot;70&quot; sandbox=&quot;allow-same-origin&quot;&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>list-style-image</b> = <b>…</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>iframe { list-style-image: …; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Number input within / outside min-max.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::first-line</code></li><li>✔ B. <code>:in-range / :out-of-range</code></li><li>C. <code>element</code></li><li>D. <code>:focus</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p997">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 998 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p999">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p999" data-page="999" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 122"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 999 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 122 — input × scroll-padding-top</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">input</span> <span class="badge prop">scroll-padding-top</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">scroll-padding-top</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;input&gt;</code> — the most versatile form control: text, email, number, date, file, checkbox, radio, range, color, search and more. Padding inside a scroll/snap container (align snapped items under headers).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;input&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><form style="display:grid;gap:8px;font-size:12px;max-width:250px"><label style="display:grid;gap:3px"><b>Full name</b><input style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></label><label style="display:grid;gap:3px"><b>Email</b><input type="email" style="border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></label><label style="display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center"><input type="checkbox" checked> Newsletter</label><button style="justify-self:start;background:#2563eb;color:#fff;border:none;border-radius:6px;padding:6px 16px">Send</button></form></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;form&gt; &lt;label&gt;Full name &lt;input type=&quot;text&quot; name=&quot;name&quot; required autocomplete=&quot;name&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;Email &lt;input type=&quot;email&quot; name=&quot;email&quot; required&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;Age &lt;input type=&quot;number&quot; name=&quot;age&quot; min=&quot;0&quot; max=&quot;120&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt; &lt;label&gt;&lt;input type=&quot;checkbox&quot; name=&quot;news&quot; checked&gt; Newsletter&lt;/label&gt; &lt;button&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt; &lt;/form&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>scroll-padding-top</b> = <b>length</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>input { scroll-padding-top: length; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “Element&#x27;s text direction matches.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>✔ A. <code>:dir(dir)</code></li><li>B. <code>::marker</code></li><li>C. <code>[attr]</code></li><li>D. <code>:first-child</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p998">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 999 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="#p1000">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <section class="page" id="p1000" data-page="1000" data-tag="drill" data-title="Drill 123"> <div class="pg-head"><span class="crumb">Part VI — The 8000 Practice Pages · Practice 1</span><span>Page 1000 of 8000</span></div> <h2>Drill 123 — label × transition-duration</h2><div class="crumb-row"><span class="badge tag">label</span> <span class="badge prop">transition-duration</span></div><p class="sum">Apply <code class="prop">transition-duration</code> to <code class="tag">&lt;label&gt;</code> — a caption for a form control — clickable, and read by screen readers. How long the transition takes (s or ms).</p><h3>1 · The element</h3><div class="demo"><div class="demo-bar"><span></span><span></span><span></span><em>&lt;label&gt; as rendered</em></div><div class="demo-body"><div style="font-size:12px;max-width:230px"><div style="display:flex;gap:8px;align-items:center"><span style="font-weight:600">Email address</span><input style="flex:1;border:1px solid #d1d5db;border-radius:6px;padding:5px 8px"></div><div style="display:flex;gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-top:8px"><input type="checkbox" checked> <span>Accept terms (wrapped label — click the text to toggle)</span></div></div></div></div><h3>2 · Starter code</h3><pre class="code"><code>&lt;label for=&quot;email&quot;&gt;Email address&lt;/label&gt; &lt;input id=&quot;email&quot; type=&quot;email&quot;&gt; &lt;label&gt;Accept terms &lt;input type=&quot;checkbox&quot; id=&quot;t&quot;&gt; &lt;/label&gt;</code></pre><h3>3 · Your task</h3><ul><li>Write one CSS rule that applies <b>transition-duration</b> = <b>time</b> to the element.</li><li>Explain (1 sentence) what changes in the browser.</li></ul><h3>4 · Solution</h3><pre class="code"><code>label { transition-duration: time; }</code></pre><h3>5 · Value quick-quiz</h3><p class="mut">What does this selector do? “The NEXT sibling, immediately after.”</p><ul class="quiz"><li>A. <code>::cue</code></li><li>B. <code>[attr$=…]</code></li><li>✔ C. <code>+</code></li><li>D. <code>:nth-child(n)</code></li></ul> <div class="pg-foot"> <a data-nav="prev" href="#p999">← Prev</a> <span class="num">Page 1000 / 8000 · Practice 1</span> <a data-nav="next" href="../volumes/vol-03.html#p1001">Next →</a> <span class="jump">Go to <input class="jump-input" type="number" min="1" max="8000" placeholder="page"> <a href="../index.html">🗺 Map</a></span> </div> </section> <script> (function(){ var pageEl = document.querySelector('.page[data-page]'); if(!pageEl) return; // hash scroll function goHash(){ if(location.hash){ var t = document.querySelector(location.hash); if(t) t.scrollIntoView(); } } window.addEventListener('load', goHash); window.addEventListener('hashchange', goHash); // keyboard document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if(e.target.matches('input,textarea')) return; if(e.key === 'ArrowRight'){ var n = document.querySelector('a[data-nav="next"]'); if(n) n.click(); } if(e.key === 'ArrowLeft'){ var p = document.querySelector('a[data-nav="prev"]'); if(p) p.click(); } }); // jump (every page has one) var boxes = document.querySelectorAll('.jump-input'); for(var bi = 0; bi < boxes.length; bi++){ (function(box){ box.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){ if(e.key !== 'Enter') return; var n = parseInt(box.value, 10); if(!n || n < 1 || n > 8000){ box.value=''; box.placeholder='1–8000'; return; } var vol = Math.ceil(n / 500); location.href = 'vol-' + String(vol).padStart(2, '0') + '.html' + '#p' + n; }); })(boxes[bi]); } })(); </script> </body> </html>
